Findings below. All line numbers are from the current worktree.

## 1. `status` pays for a full local checkpoint-store scan: one `git ls-tree` + one `git cat-file` per checkpoint, serially

`runAgentStatus` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/agent_surface.go:1063`) calls `populateBrainStatusVerification` at line 1070, which goes to `verificationSummaryForBranch` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/verify_cmd.go:904`) and then `buildVerifyReport`. The first anchor that names a checkpoint triggers `verifyContext.localCheckpointSnapshot` (`verify_cmd.go:711`) → `loadLocalCheckpointSnapshotForVerify` (`verify_cmd.go:785`) → `loadLocalCheckpointUnionSnapshot` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/export.go:1705`). That function enumerates **every** checkpoint in `refs/entire/checkpoints/*` and the aggregate refs — `loadPerCheckpointSources` runs `git ls-tree -r --name-only <ref>` once per checkpoint ref (`export.go:2003`), then the per-id loop at `export.go:1735` calls `readCheckpointSnapshotMetadata` (`export.go:1770`, body at `export.go:2174`) which issues one `git cat-file -p <ref>:<path>` per root-metadata and per session-metadata blob (`export.go:2387`, `export.go:2250`, reader at `export.go:2749`, exec at `export.go:2800`). Nothing is parallel and nothing is bounded by the fact sample: this is thousands of serial forks of git, which is exactly the "~27s sys, git spawning one at a time for the whole run" profile. The fix is to batch: one `git cat-file --batch` (or `--batch-all-objects`) process fed all metadata OIDs from a single `ls-tree -r` per ref, or at minimum a bounded worker pool, plus scoping the snapshot to the checkpoints the selected anchors actually reference rather than the whole store.

## 2. The checkpoint metadata cache exists but is disabled on exactly this path

`checkpointMetadataCache` memoizes metadata blobs by git OID and persists to `export/checkpoint-metadata-cache.json.gz` (`export.go:2656-2772`), but it is constructed only inside the export command (`export.go:177-184`). `loadLocalCheckpointSnapshotForVerify` passes `nil` for the cache (`verify_cmd.go:798`), so in `checkpointBlobReader.read` the `r.cache == nil` branch (`export.go:2754`) fires for every blob and goes straight to `git cat-file`. Worse, the OID prefetch that makes the cache usable is itself gated on `cache != nil` (`export.go:1956-1960` and `export.go:2019-2022`), so the disk cache written by `export` can never be hit by `status`/`verify` even though the blobs are byte-identical and content-addressed. Passing `loadCheckpointMetadataCache(...)` into the verify/status snapshot load is a one-line change that turns the second and subsequent `status` runs into near-zero git work for unchanged checkpoints.

## 3. Snapshot assembly is quadratic in CPU on top of the subprocess cost (the ~24s user)

For the aggregate (git-branch) backend, `loadAggregateCheckpointSources` lists the whole ref tree once and then, for every checkpoint id found in that listing, calls `pathsUnderCheckpointRoot` (`export.go:1968`) and `oidsUnderCheckpointRoot` (`export.go:1978`), each of which does a full linear scan with `strings.HasPrefix` over the entire path/OID map (`export.go:2062-2081`). With C checkpoints and P total tree paths this is O(C×P) string prefix work before a single blob is read; `readCheckpointSnapshotMetadata` then re-walks `treePaths` per checkpoint (`export.go:2180`). The same shape repeats on the query side during verification: `checkpointExistsInSnapshot` iterates all `snapshot.Sources` and `TreePaths` per anchor (`verify_cmd.go:804`), `sessionCheckpoint` linearly scans `snapshot.SessionCheckpoints` per anchor (`verify_cmd.go:736`), and `verifyExportedSession` scans all 337 manifest session rows per anchor (`verify_cmd.go:534-543`). The main issues: the delta command redundantly reads and hashes the full corpus before checking cache even though export itself is cheap; the refresh history path does two full corpus read+hash passes plus multiple re-serializations and re-hashes of the large index, and even the no-op guard re-hashes the whole corpus; the entities history command always re-scans the full checkpoint store to verify snapshots even when empty, adding unnecessary overhead.

4. git remote checks aren't used by this plugin — only origin URL lookups and a semantic repo-key regex query. ## Findings (round 2)

### 1. `refresh delta` re-reads and SHA-256s the entire 1.5GB transcript corpus before it is allowed to consult its own cache

The delta overlay build loops every exported transcript at `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/history_delta.go:307` and calls `readHistorySessionInventoryFile` at line 315 — which slurps the whole file into memory and hashes it (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/history.go:1449-1460`) — *before* the two skip checks at `history_delta.go:327` and `history_delta.go:334`. Both checks require `cached.ContentDigest == contentDigest`, so the digest must exist before either can fire; size and mtime are already in the cache entry and are compared in the same condition, but they can never short-circuit the read. That is 337 files / ~1.5GB of read + SHA-256 on every single run including a no-op second run, which is the whole 40-47s. It does **not** touch the checkpoint snapshot from `export.go`: the export half (`history_delta.go:986`, `runExport`) is the 0.8s `refresh sessions` path, and that one *does* get the metadata cache wired (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/export.go:177-184`). The fix is to gate the read on `(size, mtime)` matching the cache entry and only hash when they differ, keeping the digest as the authority exactly when the cheap identity says something moved.

### 2. `refresh history` pays the corpus hash twice and serializes/hashes the 113MB index four times; old generations *are* pruned

`prepareBrainHistoryProjectionContext` (`history.go:363`) does a metadata-only identity capture, then `buildBrainHistoryIndexSnapshotContext` reads and hashes every transcript (`history.go:1255`), and then at `history.go:381` calls `captureHistoryProjectionIdentityContext` → `includeContents=true` → a second full read+digest of the whole corpus at `history.go:1084-1093`. Record *parsing* is genuinely incremental (the scan cache is reused at `history.go:1270-1281`), so the parse is not the cost — the two mandatory corpus hashes are. On top of that the index is materialized four times over: `json.MarshalIndent` into one 113MB buffer (`history.go:395`, indenting inflates both bytes and CPU versus `Marshal`), `sha256.Sum256` of it (`history.go:398`), a second hash into `generationHash` (`history.go:402`), the staged write (`history.go:412`), a third hash via `historyIndexBytesFingerprint` (`history.go:430`), and `historyRecordsFingerprint` (`history.go:431`, body at `history.go:1141`) which re-marshals all 168171 records one at a time. There is no HEAD-keyed early-out inside `refresh history` — it always rebuilds; the only skip guard, `historyIndexCurrent` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/refresh.go:554`), is used solely by the full `refresh` (`refresh.go:298`) and is itself expensive because `collectHistorySessionDigests` (`history.go:1417-1438`) reads and hashes the whole corpus a third time. Old generations are pruned correctly (`history.go:550-558` → `pruneInactiveHistoryGenerations`, `history.go:676`), so disk does not grow unbounded. Fixes: stream-encode the index straight to the staged file through an `io.MultiWriter` that computes both digests in one pass, drop `MarshalIndent` for a machine-read artifact, derive `RecordsFingerprint` incrementally from the per-file cached digests, and reuse the build's digests for the post-scan identity check instead of re-reading the corpus.

### 3. `entities history` spends its 61s on the same full checkpoint-store scan, and does it even when the entity index is empty

`entityHistory` → `loadEntityIndexView` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/entities_cmd.go:573`) ends every path — cache hit, cache miss, stale-cache fallback — through the `finish` closure at `entities_cmd.go:591`, which unconditionally calls `sessionIDsByCheckpoint` (`entities_cmd.go:853`). That function calls `loadLocalCheckpointSnapshotForVerify` at `entities_cmd.go:868` — the exact scan from my earlier finding: one `git ls-tree` per checkpoint ref plus one `git cat-file` per metadata blob, serially, with the metadata cache passed as `nil`. With the graph plugin missing, `rebuildEntityIndexCache` returns at `entities_cmd.go:671-673` (`snapshot.Empty()`) with zero entries, so the join loop at `entities_cmd.go:598-603` iterates nothing — the entire snapshot was built to populate a map that is then applied to an empty set. A smaller add-on: `entityindex.ProviderIdentity` at `entities_cmd.go:606` shells `entire graph version --json` under a 10s timeout (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/entityindex/identity.go:28-30`), which is wasted work when the plugin is absent. Fix: return early from `finish` when `view.cache.Entries` is empty, and otherwise pass the set of checkpoint IDs actually referenced by the entries so the snapshot load can be scoped instead of enumerating the whole store.

### 4. This plugin never runs `git remote -v` — but every git call it *does* make spawns a second, uncached `git config` probe

Exhaustive search of the production Go code turns up exactly three remote-related git spawns, none of them `-v`: `git remote get-url origin` at `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/env.go:409` and `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/add.go:61`, and `git config --get-regexp ^remote\..*\.url$` at `/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/semantic_repokey.go:98`. The only `git remote -v` strings in the tree are recorded agent bash commands inside `benchmarks/agent-brain/evidence/.../record.json`, i.e. transcripts of an agent running it itself — that is the likely source of the 105 orphans, not this plugin. The shared runner is also leak-safe: `runExecCommand` uses buffered `cmd.Run()` with `cmd.WaitDelay = commandWaitDelay` (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/runner.go:75-117`, rationale at `runner.go:57-73`), and the one deliberate detach (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/setup_spawn.go:32-67`) spawns the brain worker with stdio redirected and its pid recorded. The real find here is a performance one that amplifies every serial loop above: `runExecCommand` calls `repoFilterDriverOverrides` for **every** `git` invocation (`runner.go:88-95`), and that deliberately re-enumerates config on each call with no cache (`/Users/evisdrenova/conductor/workspaces/entire-brain/regina/internal/cli/git_harden_filters.go:85-124`) — so N git operations cost 2N processes, doubling the fork/exec bill on the checkpoint snapshot scan, verify, and entities. It is also the one git spawn in the binary that sets no `WaitDelay` (`git_harden_filters.go:122-124`), so if its 5s timeout fires while a grandchild holds the pipe, `cmd.Output()` can block past the kill. A short-lived in-process memo keyed by repo dir + the stat identity of the resolved config inputs, scoped to a single command invocation, would halve the process count without weakening the chokepoint.
